Boss Babe
BAWS BAYB
noun (Millennial slang)
A self-label for an ambitious young woman running her own business, popular on Instagram from the mid-2010s, in the same family as Sophia Amoruso’s #GIRLBOSS (2014). The hashtag became especially associated with multi-level marketing (MLM) companies, whose recruiters invited women, often young mothers, to become "boss babes" by selling leggings, cosmetics, essential oils, or supplements and recruiting others. By the late 2010s the phrase was widely mocked as MLM jargon, and critics documented that most MLM participants lose money.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A boss babe is a young woman who runs her own business, or says she does: the Instagram entrepreneur with a laptop at the coffee shop, a ring light, and a link in her bio. Often she is selling for a multi-level marketing company and inviting her friends to "join her team." The Christian observation: the virtuous woman of Proverbs is, among other things, a businesswoman. "She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard" (Pro 31:16); "She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant" (Pro 31:24). Lydia was "a seller of purple" (Act 16:14). Scripture has no objection to women working with skill and earning well, ordered to the good of their households. The examination concerns the culture around the slogan. The "boss babe" image often sells independence from home as the prize and frames success as visible wealth. And the MLM version can be exploitative, turning friendships into sales targets and promising riches most participants never see. "He that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent" (Pro 28:20). The virtuous woman’s business served her household; "The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her" (Pro 31:11), and "her children arise up, and call her blessed" (Pro 31:28). A father tells his daughter: use your gifts in business if God leads you there, honestly and diligently; do not sell to your friends what you would not buy yourself; and measure success by faithfulness to your household and your Lord, not by your follower count.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial Instagram self-label (mid-2010s; MLM jargon) for an entrepreneurial young woman; Scripture honours the businesswoman of Proverbs 31 (Pro 31:16, 24), and examines the slogan’s image-selling, its MLM exploitation, and its detachment from household.

BOSS BABE, n. (Millennial social-media slang, mid-2010s–present) An ambitious woman running her own business; especially, a recruiter or seller in a multi-level-marketing company. Related: #girlboss, "join my team."

No Webster 1828 entry located for the root boss (an Americanism from Dutch baas).

Decode for parents: encourage your daughter’s gifts for work; warn her about schemes that turn friends into a sales funnel.

Key Scripture

Pro 31:16 — "She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard."

Pro 31:24 — "She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant."

Act 16:14 — "And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul."

Pro 28:20 — "A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent."

Pro 31:28 — "Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her."

Modern Corruption

Boss babe sells an image of independent wealth and is often MLM recruitment; Scripture honours the enterprising woman whose work serves her household and whose dealings are honest.

expand to see more

The corruption is image over substance. The boss-babe aesthetic, laptop, latte, luxury, sells the appearance of success, and in the MLM world the appearance is the product: recruits buy inventory to look like bosses, and most lose money. Friendships become prospect lists. The slogan also frames the household as something to escape and the market as the place of real fulfilment, which reverses the order of Proverbs 31, where enterprise serves the home.

The redemption is honest enterprise ordered to love. The virtuous woman works with her hands, trades wisely, cares for the poor, and is praised in the gates by her works rather than her posts. Teach daughters that business can be a godly calling, that honesty and quality matter more than branding, that friends are not customers, and that the deepest praise a woman can receive is the blessing of her children and the trust of her husband.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Dutch baas (master) → American boss + babe (infant; slang for a young woman) → mid-2010s Instagram boss babe → MLM jargon.
